faqs.title: What does the Islamic foundation chapter cover?
faqs.body: It explains Tawheed, the oneness of Allah, and how every act of worship roots itself in that testimony.

faqs.title: Why is Tawheed considered the foundation of Islamic faith?
faqs.body: Tawheed affirms that Allah alone deserves worship, so every belief, law, and character trait rests on that unity.

faqs.title: How should I keep the foundation alive in everyday decisions?
faqs.body: Anchor intentions in Allah, audit actions for signs of shirk, and repeat the shahada when distractions appear.

faqs.title: What are common mistakes learners make about this chapter?
faqs.body: Treating Tawheed as abstract, idolizing culture, or neglecting accountability; the chapter warns against these errors.

faqs.title: Which practices help strengthen the Islamic foundation?
faqs.body: Daily dhikr, Quran reflection on Allah's names, learning seerah highlights, and teaching others keeps the foundation firm.

faqs.title: Do we believe in original sin?
faqs.body: No. In Islam, every child is born upon the natural disposition (Fiṭrah) of Islām. No one bears the sin of another. "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another..." (Al-Anʿām 6:164)

faqs.title: Why believe in previous books if they are corrupted?
faqs.body: We believe they were originally true revelations from Allāh. We believe in what remains of truth in them but follow only the final, preserved Qur’ān as our law. "And We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it..." (Al-Māʾidah 5:48)

faqs.title: Does belief in Qadar mean we shouldn’t make effort or plan?
faqs.body: No. Belief in Qadar means taking lawful means (asbāb) while trusting the outcome to Allāh. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Take measures, for everyone is facilitated for what he has been created." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2647)

faqs.title: Are angels and jinn the same?
faqs.body: No. Angels are created from light, always obey Allāh, and have no free will like humans. Jinn are created from smokeless fire, have free will, and can be believers or disbelievers.

faqs.title: Do Muslims believe Jesus will return?
faqs.body: Yes. Part of believing in the Last Day is believing ʿĪsā (Jesus) ibn Maryam will descend before the Day of Judgment, break the cross, kill the false Messiah (Dajjāl), and rule by Islamic law. (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 155)

faqs.title: Is someone who doesn't pray still Muslim?
faqs.body: Abandoning prayer is a major sin (kabīrah) and some scholars consider it disbelief (kufr) if done out of denial or negligence. The consensus is that it nullifies one's Islam if denied as obligatory. (Majmū' al-Fatāwā, Ibn Taymiyyah)

faqs.title: Can I give zakāh to non-Muslim relatives?
faqs.body: Zakāh is specifically for Muslims in eight categories (9:60). However, you may give voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) to non-Muslim relatives to maintain family ties. (Fatāwā al-Lajnah al-Dā’imah)

faqs.title: What breaks a fast besides eating/drinking?
faqs.body: Intentional eating/drinking, sexual intercourse, vomiting deliberately, menstruation, and injections for nourishment break the fast. Unintentional acts or injections for medication are debated. (Al-Mughnī, Ibn Qudāmah)

faqs.title: Is Hajj valid if done with a loan?
faqs.body: Yes, if one is capable of repaying it. Ability (istitā'ah) includes financial and physical capacity. (Fatāwā Ibn Bāz)

faqs.title: Can women perform Hajj without a mahram?
faqs.body: The majority of scholars say a woman must be accompanied by a mahram for Hajj. Some contemporary scholars permit group travel with trustworthy women under strict conditions. (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, An-Nawawī)

faqs.title: Is the Arabic Qur'an translated or interpreted in other languages?
faqs.body: The translation of the meanings (tarjamah maʿānī) is a human interpretation to convey sense, but it is not the Qur'an itself. The only Qur'an is the Arabic revelation. Prayer must be performed in Arabic.

faqs.title: Can women recite Qur'an during menstruation?
faqs.body: Yes, they can recite from memory without touching the Muṣḥaf, according to the majority of scholars. They are only prohibited from praying and fasting during this time.

faqs.title: What is the difference between the Qur'an and Hadith Qudsī?
faqs.body: Hadith Qudsī is Allah's meaning conveyed in the Prophet's ﷺ words. The Qur'an is Allah's exact wording (Lafẓ) and meaning, a miracle in itself, and recited in prayer.

faqs.title: How do we know the order of chapters is divine?
faqs.body: The Prophet ﷺ arranged the verses within chapters by divine instruction, and he approved the general arrangement of chapters as compiled by the Companions under divine guidance.

faqs.title: Is it mandatory to read with a specific melody (Murattal/Tajwīd)?
faqs.body: Tajwīd (correct pronunciation) is obligatory to avoid changing meaning. Beautiful melodic recitation (Tartīl) is recommended but not required. "And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation." (Al-Muzzammil 73:4)

faqs.title: Why did he have multiple wives?
faqs.body: His marriages after Khadijah's death had legislative, social, and community purposes: teaching rulings, honoring widows of companions, strengthening alliances, and setting examples. They were not pursued for mere personal desire.

faqs.title: Did he perform miracles?
faqs.body: Yes, by Allah's permission, such as the splitting of the moon, water flowing from his fingers, and the Night Journey (Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj). His greatest, continuous miracle is the Qur'an.

faqs.title: How do we know his life is accurately recorded?
faqs.body: Through the rigorous historical and chain-of-transmission (Isnad) methodology of the hadith scholars, who verified reports with named narrators and documented reliability.

faqs.title: Should we celebrate his birthday (Mawlid)?
faqs.body: This is an issue of scholarly difference. The core principle is that acts of worship require proof from the Qur'an and Sunnah, and the best way to honor him is by following his authentic Sunnah.

faqs.title: Is it obligatory to love him?
faqs.body: Yes. Loving the Prophet ﷺ more than all of creation is part of complete faith (iman), as stated in the authentic hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari (15).

faqs.title: How many obligatory prayers are there?
faqs.body: Five daily prayers - Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha - each with a specific window of time.

faqs.title: How do I learn wudu and salah correctly?
faqs.body: Follow step-by-step tutorials, pray with an experienced friend, memorize the words, and repeat frequently.

faqs.title: What is khushu and how do I build it?
faqs.body: Khushu is calm focus; slow down, picture standing before Allah, and recite meanings during prayer.

faqs.title: Where do Sunnah prayers fit this chapter?
faqs.body: They supplement obligations, deepen connection, and mirror the Prophet routine in each prayer block.

faqs.title: What if I make mistakes during prayer?
faqs.body: Stay humble, perform sujud sahw when needed, ask Allah for forgiveness, and view mistakes as learning steps.

faqs.title: How do I know if my heart is diseased?
faqs.body: Signs include hardness during Qur’an recitation, lack of tears in prayer, enjoying sins, finding obedience burdensome, and holding grudges. "Then your hearts became hardened after that..." (Al-Baqarah 2:74)

faqs.title: Is feeling jealous a major sin?
faqs.body: The initial feeling (khaṭir) is not sinful if you reject it. It becomes sinful when you dwell on it, act upon it, or wish harm upon others.

faqs.title: Can music and films really affect the heart?
faqs.body: Yes, they promote heedlessness, normalize sin, and weaken spiritual sensitivity. The Prophet ﷺ said: "There will be people from my Ummah who will permit fornication, silk, alcohol, and musical instruments." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5590)

faqs.title: How to cure a hard heart?
faqs.body: 1. Increase in prostration (prayer). 2. Cry in private seeking Allah. 3. Visit the righteous sick and graveyards. 4. Remember death frequently. 5. Recite Qur’an with reflection.

faqs.title: Does depression mean my faith is weak?
faqs.body: No. Depression can be a psychological or medical condition requiring treatment. The Prophets experienced deep sadness. Seek both spiritual cures (prayer, duʿāʾ) and professional help; Islam encourages both.

faqs.title: What does the chapter say about the heart?
faqs.body: It focuses on purification, removing diseases like envy, pride, and attachment to status.

faqs.title: How do I purify my heart from envy?
faqs.body: Celebrate others, count blessings, make dua for them, and remember everything belongs to Allah.

faqs.title: What is muhasabah?
faqs.body: Self-accounting: reviewing your day, repenting, and planning improvements before sleep.

faqs.title: How do I keep the heart soft toward Allah?
faqs.body: Recite Quran, give charity, help others, and make moments of quiet reflection.

faqs.title: How does dhikr guard against spiritual diseases?
faqs.body: Frequent remembrance reinforces humility, reminds you of accountability, and calms the soul.

faqs.title: Is it mandatory to wear traditional Islamic dress?
faqs.body: The obligation is modesty covering (ḥijāb) for women and covering from navel to knee for men. Styles vary by culture but must meet Islamic requirements of looseness, opacity, and dignity.

faqs.title: How to deal with rude non-Muslims while maintaining adab?
faqs.body: Respond with better words and patience. The Prophet ﷺ endured worse in Makkah. "Repel evil with what is better..." (Al-Muʾminūn 23:96)

faqs.title: Is joking permissible in Islam?
faqs.body: Yes, but within limits: no lies, no hurting feelings, no mockery of religion, and not excessive. The Prophet ﷺ joked but only spoke truth.

faqs.title: What are the manners of disagreement among Muslims?
faqs.body: 1. Maintain good intentions. 2. Stick to evidence. 3. Respect scholars. 4. Avoid accusations. 5. Don't publicize disputes. "And do not dispute and thus lose courage..." (Al-Anfāl 8:46)

faqs.title: How to practice adab in the digital age?
faqs.body: Apply the same principles: don't spread rumors, verify before sharing, avoid vulgar language, respect others' privacy, and use time productively.

faqs.title: Are vaccines with pork-derived ingredients permissible?
faqs.body: Yes, under necessity and lack of Halal alternatives, based on the principle: "Necessities permit prohibitions." (Al-Māʾidah 5:3) The medicinal benefit outweighs the prohibition, and it's not consumed for nutrition. (Islamic Fiqh Council ruling)

faqs.title: Is cryptocurrency Halal?
faqs.body: It depends on the type and usage. Currencies like Bitcoin used as speculative assets (high volatility, no intrinsic value) are often considered Haram due to Gharar (excessive uncertainty). Those used as stable mediums of exchange may be permissible after scholarly evaluation. (Diverse scholarly opinions; consult specialists)

faqs.title: Can I work in a bank that deals with interest?
faqs.body: Working in departments directly involved in interest transactions (loans, treasury) is prohibited. Support roles (IT, security, cleaning) where one doesn't facilitate interest may be permissible with conditions, but seeking completely Halal employment is superior. (Permanent Committee for Research and Fatāwā, Saudi Arabia)

faqs.title: Is gelatin from non-Zabīḥah animals always Haram?
faqs.body: Most scholars consider it Haram as it derives from pork or improperly slaughtered animals. However, some permit gelatin if it undergoes complete chemical transformation (istihālah). The precautionary approach is to avoid it when possible. (Differing opinions among schools)

faqs.title: What if my parents insist I give them money from my interest-based salary?
faqs.body: You cannot give them Haram money. Explain gently that you want to give them pure wealth. Seek alternative Halal income to support them. Obedience to parents stops at disobeying Allah. "But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them..." (Luqmān 31:15)

faqs.title: What if my spouse doesn't pray? Can I force them?
faqs.body: You cannot force them physically. Your duty is to advise with wisdom, beautiful preaching, and gentle reminders. Continue fulfilling their rights. If they persistently abandon prayer, scholars differ on whether this nullifies the marriage; consult a local scholar for your specific case.

faqs.title: Is polygyny mandatory or recommended?
faqs.body: It is permissible under strict conditions of justice, not mandatory or generally recommended. The Qur'an says: "Then marry those that please you of women, two, three, or four. But if you fear you will not be just, then one..." (An-Nisāʾ 4:3). Most scholars say emotional justice is nearly impossible, hence the preference for monogamy.

faqs.title: How to handle interfering in-laws?
faqs.body: With patience and wisdom. Set polite boundaries while maintaining respect. The spouse should handle their own parents. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best of you is he who is best to his family." This includes managing extended family relations wisely.

faqs.title: Can a wife work outside the home?
faqs.body: Yes, with the husband's permission and conditions: 1) It doesn't neglect her primary responsibilities to home and children. 2) The work is Islamically permissible. 3) Proper hijab and gender interaction guidelines are observed. 4) Her earnings are her own property unless she chooses to contribute.

faqs.title: What about infertility or choosing not to have children?
faqs.body: Infertility is a test; seek treatment Islamically (avoid IVF with donor eggs/sperm). Adoption is encouraged but with Islamic guidelines (child retains biological lineage, non-mahram rules apply after puberty). Choosing not to have children without valid reason is discouraged as it contradicts the objectives of marriage.

faqs.title: How do we deal with major differences without splitting the community?
faqs.body: Follow the principle established by scholars: "Cooperate in matters of agreement, and excuse one another in matters of legitimate difference." Maintain brotherhood, debate with proper etiquette (adab), and avoid declaring others beyond the pale for non-creedal issues. Diversity in jurisprudence (fiqh) is a mercy.

faqs.title: Is it obligatory to live in a Muslim-majority country or community?
faqs.body: No, but it is highly recommended (mandūb) for ease of practice and community support. Muslims in minority settings have a great reward for preserving their faith and can be a powerful means of da'wah. The Prophet ﷺ praised those who remain steadfast in difficulty.

faqs.title: What is our responsibility towards non-Muslims in our society?
faqs.body: Be just, kind, and honest neighbors and citizens. Invite them to Islam with wisdom and beautiful preaching, and oppose injustice against them. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever wrongs a non-Muslim under covenant (dhimmī), or burdens them beyond their capacity, I will be his opponent on the Day of Judgment." (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 3052)

faqs.title: How can we practically help oppressed Muslims in other countries?
faqs.body:
Start with what you can sustain: sincere du'a, supporting reliable charities, truthful awareness, lawful advocacy, and effective boycotts when feasible.

  1. Make sincere du'a for them.
  2. Donate to reliable, trustworthy charities working directly on the ground.
  3. Raise awareness truthfully without sensationalism.
  4. Engage in lawful political advocacy.
  5. Boycott companies directly supporting oppression if it is effective and feasible.

"And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men, women, and children..." (An-Nisā' 4:75)

faqs.title: How do we revive community spirit in individualistic, secular societies?
faqs.body: Start with your family and local masjid: establish regular gatherings, study circles, joint iftārs (in Ramadan), and visitation schedules. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Shall I inform you of something better than the status of fasting, prayer, and charity? Making peace between people, for verily, discord is the shaver (destroyer)." (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4919) Prioritize reconciliation and collective activities.

faqs.title: How do I maintain consistency when I feel spiritually dry or unmotivated?
faqs.body:
This is normal; even the Companions experienced fluctuations. Hold to the obligatory acts and remember that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. (Qur'an 2:286)

  1. Force yourself to perform the obligatory acts.
  2. Reduce voluntary acts but do not abandon all of them; keep small, consistent deeds. (Sahih al-Bukhari 6465)
  3. Increase supplication for motivation and firmness. (Qur'an 40:60)
  4. Read or listen to inspiring Islamic reminders.
  5. Remember that with hardship comes ease, so persevere. (Qur'an 94:5-6)

faqs.title: Is it permissible to have worldly ambitions (career, education, wealth) alongside spiritual goals?
faqs.body:
Yes, with conditions. Seek the Hereafter without forgetting your share of this world and make your intention for Allah. (Qur'an 28:77; Sahih al-Bukhari 1)

  1. The intention is to serve Allah through these means by providing for family, benefiting society, and strengthening Muslims. (Sahih al-Bukhari 1)
  2. They do not lead to neglecting obligatory worship. (Qur'an 63:9)
  3. They are acquired through halal means. (Qur'an 2:172)
  4. Remain detached inwardly and ready to lose it all for Allah's sake. (Qur'an 57:20)

faqs.title: How can I measure my spiritual growth?
faqs.body:
Measure by internal signs, not just external acts. Allah looks at hearts and deeds. (Sahih Muslim 2564)

  1. Increased love for worship and decreased difficulty in performing it. (Qur'an 8:2)
  2. Quicker repentance after sins. (Qur'an 66:8)
  3. Increased concern for the Hereafter over worldly matters. (Qur'an 87:16-17)
  4. Greater humility and decreased arrogance. (Qur'an 53:32)
  5. Enhanced love for fellow Muslims and desire to benefit them. (Qur'an 49:10)

faqs.title: What if I keep repeating the same sins despite wanting to grow?
faqs.body:
Do not despair; Allah's mercy is vast and He loves repentance. (Qur'an 39:53; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2499)

  1. Do not despair, and keep returning to repentance.
  2. Analyze triggers and create avoidance strategies.
  3. Increase specific good deeds that counter that sin. (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1987)
  4. Seek righteous company that discourages the sin. (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2378)
  5. Make sincere du'a every day for protection. (Qur'an 40:60)

faqs.title: How should I prepare for the future (retirement, old age) Islamically?
faqs.body:
Plan responsibly while investing in what lasts beyond you. (Qur'an 59:18; Sahih Muslim 1631)

  1. Save halal wealth for future needs without hoarding or extravagance. (Qur'an 17:29)
  2. Invest in continuous sadaqah jariyah like a well, Islamic education, or a beneficial book. (Sahih Muslim 1631)
  3. Strengthen your relationship with Allah and increase worship as long as life continues. (Qur'an 15:99)
  4. Nurture righteous children who will pray for you after your death. (Sahih Muslim 1631)

faqs.title: What key realities about the hereafter does the chapter cover?
faqs.body: It explains death, the grave, standing before Allah, and the scales of deeds.

faqs.title: How should I prepare for the grave?
faqs.body: Live with regular repentance, maintain good deeds, and keep ties with family.

faqs.title: Why is the Day of Judgment important?
faqs.body: It restores justice, rewards the patient, and reminds us that every deed is recorded.

faqs.title: How do I balance fear and hope about akhirah?
faqs.body: Fear the consequences of sin, but keep hope in Allah's mercy by doing good.

faqs.title: What role does charity play in the hereafter?
faqs.body: Sadaqah keeps giving after we pass, so the chapter encourages consistent giving.

faqs.title: How does the chapter describe paradise?
faqs.body: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, peace, reunions with loved ones, and endless pleasure.

faqs.title: What actions open the doors of paradise?
faqs.body: Faith, prayer, charity, patience, and kindness while avoiding major sins.

faqs.title: How is hell portrayed?
faqs.body: As intense fire, regret, and punishment for rejecting truth or committing injustice.

faqs.title: How do I keep hope without ignoring warnings?
faqs.body: Remember Allah's mercy daily and live in obedience to avoid the fire.

faqs.title: What reminders keep paradise and hell relevant?
faqs.body: Visualize them during dua, read verses about them, and let them motivate ethical choices.
